answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a jade as the anchor of the cost.
